chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Muawiyah ibn Hakeem, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Atiyyah al-Aufi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), who said:

Whoever says when he leaves his house, 'In the name of Allah,' the two angels say, 'You are guided.' If he says, 'There is no power and no strength except with Allah,' they say, 'You are protected.' If he says, 'I have placed my trust in Allah,' they say, 'You are sufficiented.' Then the Shaytan says, 'How can I deal with a servant who is guided, protected, and sufficiented?'

key_terms.تَوَکَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ: I have placed my trust in Allah
key_terms.لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّه: There is no power and no strength except with Allah

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits of reciting specific dhikr phrases when leaving the house?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith highlights the efficacy of morning adhkar in securing divine assistance through the testimony of two angels. The sequential recitation of 'Bismillah,' 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah,' and 'Tawakkaltu ala Allah' grants the believer guidance (*hudayt*), protection (*wuqiyt*), and sufficiency (*kufiyat*), creating a spiritual state that baffles Shaytan. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the transformative power of verbal devotion in daily life to repel evil influences.
